title: Digital circuit simulator in Haskell (SICP 3.3)
excerpt: I have a copy of sicp, or as it is also known, The Wizard Book.11 Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs; Abelson and Sussman; mit Press; 1996.
content_html:
I have a copy of sicp, or as it is also known, The Wizard Book.1 Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs; Abelson and Sussman; mit Press; 1996. This book is widely praised, but I can’t take the time to work my way through all of it. Instead, I’m going to occasionally jump into the parts of it that look interesting.

In the previous two installations of this series, we looked at ways of implementing generic functions. In the first one, by tagging values and dispatching operations on tags. In the second case, by filling a mutable table of operation–tag pairs. We saw how these are roughly equivalent to the existing Haskell features of sum types and type classes.

Now we’ll simulate a digital circuit. The reason this is interesting is that the solution in sicp uses hidden mutable state and message-passing to make the code object-oriented. It even uses a mutable global variable for scheduling! I wasn’t sure if it would be possible to replicate that in Haskell, but as we’ll see, it can get incredibly close.

Haskell does have mutable variables

There are many ways to implement mutable state in Haskell, but to begin with, we’ll use the way that’s most similar to the sicp solution: IORefs. An IORef is a mutable variable, like in any other programming language.2 The only major difference is that we need a bit of extra machinery to read from it, because it’s designed so that we cannot accidentally read from it in pure code. (That would make the code impure, after all.)

We define a type Wire, which starts out with its signal Low, and with an empty list of action procedures.

The idea of action procedures comes from the sicp implementation of this code; action procedures are subscribers to the signal on this wire, and they will be invoked whenever the signal changes. Action procedures will be installed by components connected downstream of this wire, so those components can update themselves when the wire value changes. 

data Signal = Low | High
  deriving (Show, Eq, Ord, Bounded)

data Wire = Wire
  { action_procedures :: IORef [IO ()]
  , signal_value      :: IORef Signal
  }

make_wire = do
  initial_procs <- newIORef []
  initial_signal <- newIORef Low
  pure (Wire initial_procs initial_signal)

We can get the signal from a wire by reading the mutable variable holding its current signal. 

get_signal (Wire _ signal) =
  readIORef signal

To set a signal on a wire we write to the mutable variable. If this causes a state change of the wire, we’ll also run the installed action procedures to let downstream components know.3 This is the observer pattern, in case it sounds familiar. 

set_signal (Wire procs signal) new_value = do
  current <- readIORef signal
  when (new_value /= current) $ do
    writeIORef signal new_value
    actions <- readIORef procs
    sequence_ actions

Finally, we have a method on the wire that lets downstream components install new action procedures. To ensure wires are initialised with the proper value when components are connected, we immediately run all action procedures we install. 

add_action (Wire procs _) action = do
  modifyIORef procs (action:)
  action

A probe in the sicp implementation is an action procedure installed on a wire that reports the value of the wire to the user of the program. 

probe name wire =
  add_action wire $ do
    current <- get_signal wire
    putStrLn (name <> " new value: " <> show current)

At this point the wire object is done, and we can experiment with it in the repl. We create a wire and add a probe to it. If we set its signal to the same thing it was before, nothing changes. If we set its signal to a new value, the probe fires. 

λ> w <- make_wire
λ> probe "wire" w
wire new value: Low
λ> set_signal w Low
λ> set_signal w High
wire new value: High

Then we can start to implement the most basic components. An inverter is, as in the sicp implementation, an action procedure on the input wire that sets the signal on its output wire to the opposite of the input. 

inverter input output =
  add_action input $ do
    current <- get_signal input
    set_signal output $ case current of
      Low  -> High
      High -> Low

The and_gate works similarly, except it reads two inputs before determining its output. 

and_gate a1 a2 output =
  let
    action = do
      c1 <- get_signal a1
      c2 <- get_signal a2
      set_signal output $ case (c1, c2) of
        (Low, Low)   -> Low
        (Low, High)  -> Low
        (High, High) -> High
        (High, Low)  -> Low
  in do
    add_action a1 action
    add_action a2 action

The or_gate is like the and_gate except with a different truth table.4 Like a true designer of digital circuits, I have put the truth table in Grey code. 

or_gate a1 a2 output =
  let
    action = do
      c1 <- get_signal a1
      c2 <- get_signal a2
      set_signal output $ case (c1, c2) of
        (Low, Low)   -> Low
        (Low, High)  -> High
        (High, High) -> High
        (High, Low)  -> High
  in do
    add_action a1 action
    add_action a2 action

So far, we have invented nothing here; this is all in line with the implementation from sicp. There are three neat properties of this Abelson and Sussman design:

  • The set of components is open. If we turn this into a library, any user of the library can add their own components and their components would interact beautifully with those we have.
  • The components are not limited to a fixed number of inputs or outputs. Anything that reads from wires and writes to other wires is a valid component.
  • We can compose these basic gates into higher-level components, as plain procedure statements.

The latter means that we can make a half-adder by composing gates, and a full-adder by composing half-adders and gates. 

half_adder a b s c = do
  d <- make_wire
  e <- make_wire
  or_gate a b d
  and_gate a b c
  inverter c e
  and_gate d e s

full_adder a b c_in sum c_out = do
  s <- make_wire
  c1 <- make_wire
  c2 <- make_wire
  half_adder b c_in s c1
  half_adder a s sum c2
  or_gate c1 c2 c_out

This all comes straight out of the sicp implementation. The only thing we’re missing so far is a scheduler to simulate propagation delay.

Adding a scheduler with global mutable state

In sicp, the scheduler is implemented as a global mutable variable. This lets any component implicitly access it for scheduling. Let’s go all in and do it that way in Haskell too.

Wait, can Haskell even do that?

Yeah. Look at the last line where we define the_agenda. Yuck! Please never do this in production. Global mutable state is a terrible idea.5 It’s a terrible idea in any programming language. But it’s even worse in Haskell, because then we’re opting out of a bunch of extra guarantees only Haskell can give us. 

data Agenda = Agenda
  { current_time :: IORef Int
  , segments     :: IORef (Map.Map Int [IO ()])
  }

make_agenda = do
  time <- newIORef 0
  segs <- newIORef Map.empty
  pure (Agenda time segs)

the_agenda = unsafePerformIO make_agenda

The agenda follows the implementation in sicp, and maintains mutable variables for the current time as well as an ordered list of times and the action procedures scheduled for those times.6 In sicp they use a linked list with some manual bookkeeping to keep it ordered. We could do that in Haskell too, but here we are lazy and use a standard-library ordered dictionary instead.

The propagate function uses this agenda to simulate the circuit until it stabilises. It pops the smallest next time step from the agenda, updates the current time to it, and executes the actions associated with it. It repeats this until there are no more scheduled time steps. 

propagate = do
  segs <- readIORef (segments the_agenda)
  case Map.minViewWithKey segs of
    Nothing -> pure ()
    Just ((time, actions), remaining) -> do
      writeIORef (current_time the_agenda) time
      writeIORef (segments the_agenda) remaining
      sequence_ actions
      propagate

The sicp code has an after_delay function to help components schedule their updates after their respective propagation delays. We’ll implement the same. 

after_delay delay action = do
  time <- readIORef (current_time the_agenda)
  modifyIORef (segments the_agenda) $
    Map.insertWith (<>) (delay + time) [action]

Now components need to use this, so they update their outputs only after a delay, rather than immediately. This means inserting an after_delay call before set_signal in all components. Here it is for the inverter, as an example. 

inverter input output =
  add_action input $ do
    current <- get_signal input
    after_delay 2 $ do
      set_signal output $ case current of
        Low  -> High
        High -> Low

We also want the probe to show the current time when it makes a reading. 

probe name wire =
  add_action wire $ do
    current <- get_signal wire
    time <- readIORef (current_time the_agenda)
    putStrLn (name <> " (t=" <> show time <> ") new value: " <> show current)

And that’s it! Now that we’re done, we can open the repl and run the same interaction as Abelson and Sussman, to test that our code behaves the same way the sicp code does. 

λ> input_1 <- make_wire
λ> input_2 <- make_wire
λ> sum <- make_wire
λ> carry <- make_wire
λ> probe "sum" sum
sum (t=0) new value: Low

λ> probe "carry" carry
carry (t=0) new value: Low

λ> half_adder input_1 input_2 sum carry

λ> set_signal input_1 High
λ> propagate
sum (t=8) new value: High

λ> set_signal input_2 High
λ> propagate
carry (t=11) new value: High
sum (t=16) new value: Low

It actually surprised me how close the Haskell solution got to the one in sicp. It’s pretty much the same thing. The only major difference I can think of is that since the_agenda is a top-level binding in Haskell, we cannot reassign it in the repl. But that’s about it.

We can also do something fun the sicp authors never showed: a ring oscillator. If we connect the output of the inverter to itself, probe it, and then propagate, we get an infinite sequence of 

--------------- >8 -------
a (t=4558) new value: High
a (t=4560) new value: Low
a (t=4560) new value: High
a (t=4562) new value: Low
a (t=4562) new value: High
a (t=4564) new value: Low
a (t=4564) new value: High
a (t=4566) new value: Low
a (t=4566) new value: High
a (t=4568) new value: Low
--------------- >8 -------

where the output toggles every propagation delay.

Next challenge: making it pure

The code above is fine. It is rife with side-effects, but it is fine.

Many people seem to have this view that Haskell code must be free of side effects, and that’s not true. Haskell code doesn’t need to be a pristine pure tower of abstraction connected to a dirty effectful layer. Haskell code can be like code in any other language – mostly dirty and effectful – but with some islands of purity where they help. That’s a legal way to use Haskell, and it’s still an improvement over other languages.

But what if we want to make the simulation pure? One way to do it would be to move the wire state management from IO to ST. While IO is a type of computation that allows arbitrary side effects, ST is a type of computation that only allows mutable variables, and it’s designed so that no effects can escape outside of its local context. That means we could execute ST-based mutation inside the circuit simulation in a way that is pure from the outside. This would be a fairly mundane transformation and is not interesting.

But Haskell lets us do even better. That’ll be a separate article. Stay tuned.

blocks.html_en: To set a signal on a wire we write to the mutable variable. If this causes a state change of the wire, we’ll also run the installed action procedures to let downstream components know.3 This is the observer pattern, in case it sounds familiar.

sentences.en: To set a signal on a wire we write to the mutable variable.
sentences.zh: 为了在电线上设置信号，我们写入可变变量。

sentences.en: If this causes a state change of the wire, we’ll also run the installed action procedures to let downstream components know.33 This is the observer pattern, in case it sounds familiar.
sentences.zh: 如果这导致线路状态发生变化，我们还将运行已安装的操作程序，让下游组件知道。33 这就是观察者模式，以防听起来很熟悉。

blocks.html_en: Finally, we have a method on the wire that lets downstream components install new action procedures. To ensure wires are initialised with the proper value when components are connected, we immediately run all action procedures we install.

sentences.en: Finally, we have a method on the wire that lets downstream components install new action procedures.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们有一个在线方法，可以让下游组件安装新的操作过程。

sentences.en: To ensure wires are initialised with the proper value when components are connected, we immediately run all action procedures we install.
sentences.zh: 为了确保在连接组件时将电线初始化为正确的值，我们立即运行我们安装的所有操作程序。

blocks.html_en: A probe in the sicp implementation is an action procedure installed on a wire that reports the value of the wire to the user of the program.

sentences.en: A probe in the sicp implementation is an action procedure installed on a wire that reports the value of the wire to the user of the program.
sentences.zh: Sicp 实现中的探针是安装在线路上的操作过程，用于向程序用户报告线路的值。

blocks.html_en: At this point the wire object is done, and we can experiment with it in the repl. We create a wire and add a probe to it. If we set its signal to the same thing it was before, nothing changes. If we set its signal to a new value, the probe fires.

sentences.zh: 我们创建一条电线并向其添加一个探针。

sentences.zh: 如果我们将其信号设置为与之前相同的信号，则不会发生任何变化。

sentences.zh: 如果我们将其信号设置为新值，探测器就会触发。

blocks.html_en: Then we can start to implement the most basic components. An inverter is, as in the sicp implementation, an action procedure on the input wire that sets the signal on its output wire to the opposite of the input.

sentences.en: Then we can start to implement the most basic components.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以开始实现最基本的组件了。

sentences.en: An inverter is, as in the sicp implementation, an action procedure on the input wire that sets the signal on its output wire to the opposite of the input.
sentences.zh: 正如在 sicp 实现中一样，反相器是输入线上的一个动作过程，它将其输出线上的信号设置为与输入相反的信号。

blocks.html_en: The and_gate works similarly, except it reads two inputs before determining its output.

sentences.en: The and_gate works similarly, except it reads two inputs before determining its output.
sentences.zh: and_gate 的工作原理类似，只是它在确定输出之前读取两个输入。

blocks.html_en: The or_gate is like the and_gate except with a different truth table.4 Like a true designer of digital circuits, I have put the truth table in Grey code.

blocks.html_en: So far, we have invented nothing here; this is all in line with the implementation from sicp. There are three neat properties of this Abelson and Sussman design:

sentences.en: So far, we have invented nothing here; this is all in line with the implementation from sicp.

sentences.en: There are three neat properties of this Abelson and Sussman design:
sentences.zh: Abelson 和 Sussman 的设计具有三个巧妙的特性：

blocks.html_en: • The set of components is open. If we turn this into a library, any user of the library can add their own components and their components would interact beautifully with those we have.

sentences.en: The set of components is open.
sentences.zh: 该组组件是开放的。

blocks.html_en: • The components are not limited to a fixed number of inputs or outputs. Anything that reads from wires and writes to other wires is a valid component.

blocks.html_en: • We can compose these basic gates into higher-level components, as plain procedure statements.

blocks.html_en: The latter means that we can make a half-adder by composing gates, and a full-adder by composing half-adders and gates.

blocks.html_en: The agenda follows the implementation in sicp, and maintains mutable variables for the current time as well as an ordered list of times and the action procedures scheduled for those times.6 In sicp they use a linked list with some manual bookkeeping to keep it ordered. We could do that in Haskell too, but here we are lazy and use a standard-library ordered dictionary instead.

sentences.zh: 我们也可以在 Haskell 中做到这一点，但这里我们很懒，而是使用标准库有序字典。

blocks.html_en: The propagate function uses this agenda to simulate the circuit until it stabilises. It pops the smallest next time step from the agenda, updates the current time to it, and executes the actions associated with it. It repeats this until there are no more scheduled time steps.

sentences.en: The propagate function uses this agenda to simulate the circuit until it stabilises.
sentences.zh: 传播函数使用此议程来模拟电路，直到其稳定。

sentences.en: It pops the smallest next time step from the agenda, updates the current time to it, and executes the actions associated with it.
sentences.zh: 它从议程中弹出最小的下一个时间步骤，将当前时间更新为它，并执行与其关联的操作。

sentences.en: It repeats this until there are no more scheduled time steps.
sentences.zh: 它会重复此操作，直到不再有计划的时间步。

blocks.html_en: The sicp code has an after_delay function to help components schedule their updates after their respective propagation delays. We’ll implement the same.

blocks.html_en: Now components need to use this, so they update their outputs only after a delay, rather than immediately. This means inserting an after_delay call before set_signal in all components. Here it is for the inverter, as an example.

blocks.html_en: We also want the probe to show the current time when it makes a reading.

sentences.en: We also want the probe to show the current time when it makes a reading.

blocks.html_en: And that’s it! Now that we’re done, we can open the repl and run the same interaction as Abelson and Sussman, to test that our code behaves the same way the sicp code does.

sentences.en: Now that we’re done, we can open the repl and run the same interaction as Abelson and Sussman, to test that our code behaves the same way the sicp code does.

blocks.html_en: It actually surprised me how close the Haskell solution got to the one in sicp. It’s pretty much the same thing. The only major difference I can think of is that since the_agenda is a top-level binding in Haskell, we cannot reassign it in the repl. But that’s about it.

sentences.en: It actually surprised me how close the Haskell solution got to the one in sicp.
sentences.zh: 事实上，让我惊讶的是 Haskell 的解决方案与 sicp 中的解决方案如此接近。

sentences.en: It’s pretty much the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是同一件事。

sentences.en: The only major difference I can think of is that since the_agenda is a top-level binding in Haskell, we cannot reassign it in the repl.
sentences.zh: 我能想到的唯一主要区别是，由于 the_agenda 是 Haskell 中的顶级绑定，因此我们无法在 repl 中重新分配它。

sentences.en: But that’s about it.

blocks.html_en: We can also do something fun the sicp authors never showed: a ring oscillator. If we connect the output of the inverter to itself, probe it, and then propagate, we get an infinite sequence of

blocks.html_en: where the output toggles every propagation delay.

blocks.html_en: Next challenge: making it pure

blocks.html_en: The code above is fine. It is rife with side-effects, but it is fine.

blocks.html_en: Many people seem to have this view that Haskell code must be free of side effects, and that’s not true. Haskell code doesn’t need to be a pristine pure tower of abstraction connected to a dirty effectful layer. Haskell code can be like code in any other language – mostly dirty and effectful – but with some islands of purity where they help. That’s a legal way to use Haskell, and it’s still an improvement over other languages.

sentences.en: Many people seem to have this view that Haskell code must be free of side effects, and that’s not true.
sentences.zh: 许多人似乎认为 Haskell 代码必须没有副作用，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Haskell code doesn’t need to be a pristine pure tower of abstraction connected to a dirty effectful layer.
sentences.zh: Haskell 代码不需要是连接到肮脏的有效层的原始纯粹抽象塔。

sentences.en: Haskell code can be like code in any other language – mostly dirty and effectful – but with some islands of purity where they help.
sentences.zh: Haskell 代码可以像任何其他语言中的代码一样 - 大部分是脏的和有效的 - 但有一些纯粹的岛屿可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: That’s a legal way to use Haskell, and it’s still an improvement over other languages.
sentences.zh: 这是使用 Haskell 的合法方式，而且它仍然比其他语言有所改进。

blocks.html_en: But what if we want to make the simulation pure? One way to do it would be to move the wire state management from IO to ST. While IO is a type of computation that allows arbitrary side effects, ST is a type of computation that only allows mutable variables, and it’s designed so that no effects can escape outside of its local context. That means we could execute ST-based mutation inside the circuit simulation in a way that is pure from the outside. This would be a fairly mundane transformation and is not interesting.

sentences.en: But what if we want to make the simulation pure?

sentences.en: One way to do it would be to move the wire state management from IO to ST.
sentences.zh: 一种方法是将线路状态管理从 IO 移至 ST。

sentences.en: While IO is a type of computation that allows arbitrary side effects, ST is a type of computation that only allows mutable variables, and it’s designed so that no effects can escape outside of its local context.
sentences.zh: IO 是一种允许任意副作用的计算类型，而 ST 是一种只允许可变变量的计算类型，并且它的设计使得任何效果都无法逃脱其本地上下文之外。

sentences.en: That means we could execute ST-based mutation inside the circuit simulation in a way that is pure from the outside.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们可以在电路模拟内部以纯粹从外部的方式执行基于 ST 的突变。

sentences.en: This would be a fairly mundane transformation and is not interesting.
sentences.zh: 这将是一个相当平凡的转变，而且并不有趣。

content_html_zh:
我有一本 sicp，或者也称为 The Wizard Book.11 计算机程序的结构和解释；阿贝尔森和萨斯曼；麻省理工学院出版社； 1996年。 这本书广受好评，但我无法花时间读完这本书。 相反，我偶尔会跳到其中看起来有趣的部分。

在本系列的前两次安装中，我们研究了实现通用函数的方法。 在第一个中，通过标记值并在标签上分派操作。 在第二种情况下，通过填充操作标签对的可变表。 我们看到它们与现有的和类型和类型类的 Haskell 功能大致相同。

现在我们将模拟数字电路。 这很有趣的原因是 sicp 中的解决方案使用隐藏的可变状态和消息传递来使代码面向对象。 它甚至使用可变的全局变量来进行调度！ 我不确定是否可以在 Haskell 中复制它，但正如我们将看到的，它可以非常接近。

Haskell 确实有可变变量

在 Haskell 中实现可变状态的方法有很多，但首先，我们将使用与 sicp 解决方案最相似的方法：IORefs。 IORef 是一个可变变量，就像任何其他编程语言一样。22 唯一的主要区别是我们需要一些额外的机制来读取它，因为它的设计使我们不会意外地在纯代码中读取它。 （毕竟，这会使代码变得不纯净。）

我们定义了一个 Wire 类型，它以 Low 信号开始，并带有一个空的操作过程列表。

动作过程的思想来自于该代码的 sicp 实现；操作过程是该线路上信号的订阅者，只要信号发生变化，它们就会被调用。 操作过程将由连接到该连线下游的组件安装，因此当连线值发生更改时，这些组件可以自行更新。

data Signal = Low | High
  deriving (Show, Eq, Ord, Bounded)

data Wire = Wire
  { action_procedures :: IORef [IO ()]
  , signal_value      :: IORef Signal
  }

make_wire = do
  initial_procs <- newIORef []
  initial_signal <- newIORef Low
  pure (Wire initial_procs initial_signal)

我们可以通过读取保存当前信号的可变变量来从电线获取信号。

get_signal (Wire _ signal) =
  readIORef signal

为了在电线上设置信号，我们写入可变变量。 如果这导致线路状态发生变化，我们还将运行已安装的操作程序，让下游组件知道。33 这就是观察者模式，以防听起来很熟悉。

set_signal (Wire procs signal) new_value = do
  current <- readIORef signal
  when (new_value /= current) $ do
    writeIORef signal new_value
    actions <- readIORef procs
    sequence_ actions

最后，我们有一个在线方法，可以让下游组件安装新的操作过程。 为了确保在连接组件时将电线初始化为正确的值，我们立即运行我们安装的所有操作程序。

add_action (Wire procs _) action = do
  modifyIORef procs (action:)
  action

Sicp 实现中的探针是安装在线路上的操作过程，用于向程序用户报告线路的值。

probe name wire =
  add_action wire $ do
    current <- get_signal wire
    putStrLn (name <> " new value: " <> show current)

至此，wire 对象就完成了，我们可以在 repl 中对其进行实验。 我们创建一条电线并向其添加一个探针。 如果我们将其信号设置为与之前相同的信号，则不会发生任何变化。 如果我们将其信号设置为新值，探测器就会触发。

λ> w <- make_wire
λ> probe "wire" w
wire new value: Low
λ> set_signal w Low
λ> set_signal w High
wire new value: High

然后我们就可以开始实现最基本的组件了。 正如在 sicp 实现中一样，反相器是输入线上的一个动作过程，它将其输出线上的信号设置为与输入相反的信号。

inverter input output =
  add_action input $ do
    current <- get_signal input
    set_signal output $ case current of
      Low  -> High
      High -> Low

and_gate 的工作原理类似，只是它在确定输出之前读取两个输入。

and_gate a1 a2 output =
  let
    action = do
      c1 <- get_signal a1
      c2 <- get_signal a2
      set_signal output $ case (c1, c2) of
        (Low, Low)   -> Low
        (Low, High)  -> Low
        (High, High) -> High
        (High, Low)  -> Low
  in do
    add_action a1 action
    add_action a2 action

or_gate 与 and_gate 类似，只是具有不同的真值表。44 像真正的数字电路设计者一样，我将真值表放入格雷码中。

or_gate a1 a2 output =
  let
    action = do
      c1 <- get_signal a1
      c2 <- get_signal a2
      set_signal output $ case (c1, c2) of
        (Low, Low)   -> Low
        (Low, High)  -> High
        (High, High) -> High
        (High, Low)  -> High
  in do
    add_action a1 action
    add_action a2 action

到目前为止，我们还没有发明任何东西；这完全符合sicp的实施。 Abelson 和 Sussman 的设计具有三个巧妙的特性：

  • 该组组件是开放的。 如果我们将其变成一个库，该库的任何用户都可以添加自己的组件，并且他们的组件将与我们拥有的组件完美地交互。
  • 这些组件不限于固定数量的输入或输出。 任何从线路读取数据并写入其他线路的组件都是有效组件。
  • 我们可以将这些基本门组合成更高级别的组件，作为简单的过程语句。

后者意味着我们可以通过组成门来组成半加器，通过半加器和门组成全加器。

half_adder a b s c = do
  d <- make_wire
  e <- make_wire
  or_gate a b d
  and_gate a b c
  inverter c e
  and_gate d e s

full_adder a b c_in sum c_out = do
  s <- make_wire
  c1 <- make_wire
  c2 <- make_wire
  half_adder b c_in s c1
  half_adder a s sum c2
  or_gate c1 c2 c_out

这一切都直接来自 sicp 实现。 到目前为止，我们唯一缺少的是模拟传播延迟的调度程序。

添加具有全局可变状态的调度程序

在 sicp 中，调度程序被实现为全局可变变量。 这允许任何组件隐式访问它以进行调度。 让我们全力以赴，在 Haskell 中也这样做。

等等，Haskell 能做到吗？

是的。 看一下我们定义 the_agenda 的最后一行。 哎呀！ 请永远不要在生产中这样做。 全局可变状态是一个糟糕的想法。55 对于任何编程语言来说，这都是一个糟糕的想法。 但在 Haskell 中情况更糟，因为这样我们就选择退出只有 Haskell 才能给我们的一系列额外保证。

data Agenda = Agenda
  { current_time :: IORef Int
  , segments     :: IORef (Map.Map Int [IO ()])
  }

make_agenda = do
  time <- newIORef 0
  segs <- newIORef Map.empty
  pure (Agenda time segs)

the_agenda = unsafePerformIO make_agenda

议程遵循 sicp 中的实现，并维护当前时间的可变变量以及时间的有序列表和为这些时间安排的操作程序。66 在 sicp 中，他们使用链接列表和一些手动簿记来保持有序。 我们也可以在 Haskell 中做到这一点，但这里我们很懒，而是使用标准库有序字典。

传播函数使用此议程来模拟电路，直到其稳定。 它从议程中弹出最小的下一个时间步骤，将当前时间更新为它，并执行与其关联的操作。 它会重复此操作，直到不再有计划的时间步。

propagate = do
  segs <- readIORef (segments the_agenda)
  case Map.minViewWithKey segs of
    Nothing -> pure ()
    Just ((time, actions), remaining) -> do
      writeIORef (current_time the_agenda) time
      writeIORef (segments the_agenda) remaining
      sequence_ actions
      propagate

sicp 代码有一个 after_delay 函数，可以帮助组件在各自的传播延迟后安排更新。 我们将实施相同的措施。

after_delay delay action = do
  time <- readIORef (current_time the_agenda)
  modifyIORef (segments the_agenda) $
    Map.insertWith (<>) (delay + time) [action]

现在组件需要使用它，因此它们仅在延迟后更新其输出，而不是立即更新。 这意味着在所有组件中的 set_signal 之前插入 after_delay 调用。 这里以逆变器为例。

inverter input output =
  add_action input $ do
    current <- get_signal input
    after_delay 2 $ do
      set_signal output $ case current of
        Low  -> High
        High -> Low

我们还希望探头在进行读数时显示当前时间。

probe name wire =
  add_action wire $ do
    current <- get_signal wire
    time <- readIORef (current_time the_agenda)
    putStrLn (name <> " (t=" <> show time <> ") new value: " <> show current)

就是这样！ 现在我们已经完成了，我们可以打开 repl 并运行与 Abelson 和 Sussman 相同的交互，以测试我们的代码的行为是否与 sicp 代码相同。

λ> input_1 <- make_wire
λ> input_2 <- make_wire
λ> sum <- make_wire
λ> carry <- make_wire
λ> probe "sum" sum
sum (t=0) new value: Low

λ> probe "carry" carry
carry (t=0) new value: Low

λ> half_adder input_1 input_2 sum carry

λ> set_signal input_1 High
λ> propagate
sum (t=8) new value: High

λ> set_signal input_2 High
λ> propagate
carry (t=11) new value: High
sum (t=16) new value: Low

事实上，让我惊讶的是 Haskell 的解决方案与 sicp 中的解决方案如此接近。 这几乎是同一件事。 我能想到的唯一主要区别是，由于 the_agenda 是 Haskell 中的顶级绑定，因此我们无法在 repl 中重新分配它。 但仅此而已。

我们还可以做一些 sicp 作者从未展示过的有趣的事情：环形振荡器。 如果我们将逆变器的输出连接到自身，探测它，然后传播，我们会得到一个无限序列

--------------- >8 -------
a (t=4558) new value: High
a (t=4560) new value: Low
a (t=4560) new value: High
a (t=4562) new value: Low
a (t=4562) new value: High
a (t=4564) new value: Low
a (t=4564) new value: High
a (t=4566) new value: Low
a (t=4566) new value: High
a (t=4568) new value: Low
--------------- >8 -------

其中输出切换每个传播延迟。

下一个挑战：使其纯净

上面的代码没问题。 它充满了副作用，但没关系。

许多人似乎认为 Haskell 代码必须没有副作用，但事实并非如此。 Haskell 代码不需要是连接到肮脏的有效层的原始纯粹抽象塔。 Haskell 代码可以像任何其他语言中的代码一样 - 大部分是脏的和有效的 - 但有一些纯粹的岛屿可以提供帮助。 这是使用 Haskell 的合法方式，而且它仍然比其他语言有所改进。

但是如果我们想让模拟变得纯粹怎么办？ 一种方法是将线路状态管理从 IO 移至 ST。 IO 是一种允许任意副作用的计算类型，而 ST 是一种只允许可变变量的计算类型，并且它的设计使得任何效果都无法逃脱其本地上下文之外。 这意味着我们可以在电路模拟内部以纯粹从外部的方式执行基于 ST 的突变。 这将是一个相当平凡的转变，而且并不有趣。

但 Haskell 让我们做得更好。 这将是一篇单独的文章。 敬请关注。
